seekers.source: ACS 2020-2024 five-year PUMS, person file, 55 NYC PUMAs (scripts/fetch_census_pums.py)
seekers.geography: five boroughs only; postings span the NY metro (known mismatch, read as commuting)
seekers.group_cutoff_rule: person-weighted median WAGP*ADJINC of all NYC seekers in the frame
seekers.group_cutoff_value: 58,656.82 in 2024 dollars (WAGP x ADJINC; weighted median of the 136,835-record frame, computed 2026-11-21 by hiddenoptions.jobs.markets.load_seekers). The code compares in 2024 dollars, not July 2026 dollars as group_variable says; the split is the same either way because one CPI factor scales every seeker

donor_partition.use: calibration configs use donors=calibration; pilot used all; frozen comparison uses evaluation

seekers.experience_proxy: min((AGEP - 22) // 6, 6) on the 1..7 seniority scale; modeled, crude

pums_occupation_codes.wildcards: X and a sixth-digit 0 (broad occupation) match any detailed code under them
pums_occupation_codes.533032: seekers coded 533030 (driver/sales workers and truck drivers); 2,710
pums_occupation_codes.412031: exact; 3,933 (412010 cashiers is a separate broad code)

dollars.convention: posting month: ACS 2024 dollars x CPI-U(posting month)/CPI-U(2024 annual average)

primary.occupation: 6-digit SOC match, PUMS wildcards as above
primary.pay: posted salary midpoint >= 0.8 x prior wage
primary.education: dropped: extract has no education field
primary.location: NY metro (finest field in the extract); remote_type kept: Fully In Office, Partially In Office

sensitivity.superseded: symmetric |gap| <= 2 left 47% of higher-wage seekers with no option

feasibility.capacity: one opening per posting; expected_hires (predicted, capped at 5) is a sensitivity via slot expansion

preferences.seeker_score: w_w log(s/W) + w_q Q - w_f fit + sigma_r eps; Q = standardized log salary + 0.5 x common shock; fit = |level gap| capped at 2

calibration.markets: natural, 64 per side, calibration donors, dev months, seeds 1000-1019
calibration.target: Atlanta Fed Wage Growth Tracker, job switchers, p25/p50/p75 (national; known mismatch)
calibration.target_construction: see targets in configs/jobs_calibrate.json: switcher median, with p25/p75 from all-worker gaps; tracker growth is 100*ln, so target = g/100
calibration.status: not run before freezing. Run 2026-11-21 after the frozen comparison: selects w_wage 1, seeker_noise 1.25 (grid corner), loss 0.339 vs 0.358 at the frozen (2, 0.75); loss ranges 0.339-0.370 over the grid. Every setting puts the lower-wage median log raise near +0.56 vs a +0.04 target, so the misfit comes from the feasibility rule and the ACS-annual-wage vs posted-salary comparison, not from the weights. Results: results/jobs_calibration/

selected.status: UNCALIBRATED: pilot values, frozen without running calibrate.py; report as such

preferences.employer_priority: 1.0 x 1[prior wage in 0.8 min .. 1.2 max] + 0.5 x 1[experience >= seniority] + eta; no education term

shortlist_policies.k: min(5, feasible postings); q50 arm shows ceil(0.5 x feasible); report q50 or degree-stratified alongside k = 5
shortlist_policies.comparator_for_llm: transparent (the honest relevance ranker), not uniform

later_additions.note: Analyses implemented after the frozen comparison ran (2026-11-15). None makes API calls; all reuse the saved GPT answers. Their status differs: (a) protocol-specified estimands: T, the group switch (S_L + S_H = T) and the protection premium are named in EXPERIMENT_SETUP.md (Analyses; group switch there since 2026-11-09) and the housing protocol before the jobs freeze, and the jobs setup names the protocol primary contrast for its main exhibit; only their jobs code came later. (b) Fixed before the held-out replication: accuracy, protection premium, recommendation profile, capacity/anchor and calibration were all committed by 2026-11-21 23:30 ET, before the first replication request (23:39 ET), so on 2025-11/12 they are tests specified in advance. (c) Post hoc on both windows: the T and group-switch scripts, calibrated T, one firm per seeker and the 10,000-draw rerun (2026-11-22). Frozen-month results of (b) and (c) are exploratory.
